lead.headline: Ship attacks near Hormuz keep rising, and we expect another vessel to be hit by 1 November

argument.text: Attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz reached a record this week and mines are now disabling tankers, so the risk comes from the sea itself and not from one actor, which makes a quick end to the strikes unlikely.
argument.label: judgment

happened.text: BBC Verify counted 12 vessels struck in a week, and Iran says two more tankers caught fire after hitting mines.

sources.topicId: Ship Attacks Near Hormuz Reach Record High as Oil Exports Slow-1
Iran Says Two Tankers Catch Fire After Hitting Mines in Strait of Hormuz-6

expect.text: We expect another vessel to be struck or to hit a mine by 1 November, with a probability of 80%.
expect.label: judgment

wouldProveWrong.condition: No further vessel is struck or hits a mine near Hormuz, most likely because traffic through the strait has stopped.

moved.title: Trump's Russia sanctions pause
moved.before: the open question was whether Russia would honour the 'energy ceasefire' Trump announced.
moved.after: the open question is whether Trump's pause on the new Russia sanctions package stays in force through the midterms.

mechanism.text: A week ago the question was whether Russia would honour Trump's 'energy ceasefire'; Ukraine declared it over on 15 October and Trump suspended new Russia sanctions on Friday, so we now expect the pause to last through the midterms, as he wants cheaper diesel and Congress has only criticised it.
mechanism.label: judgment
